target.title: fix(google-oauth): cancel unread response body on non-ok HTTP responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two response body leaks in Google OAuth project operations where HTTP error responses with unread bodies could keep the connection open until idle timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the polling loop or onboardUser endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body stream is not consumed before continuing or throwing. Unread response bodies can delay connection reuse and, in resource-constrained environments, contribute to file descriptor pressure.

The fix adds `response.body?.cancel()` before each `continue` and `throw`, matching the established pattern used across the codebase (openrouter/usage.ts, chutes/oauth.ts, lmstudio/models.fetch.ts, and others).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Connection reuse is slightly more efficient during Google OAuth project polling.

## Evidence

- Verified the pattern matches existing usage in `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts:133`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts:106`, and `extensions/lmstudio/src/models.fetch.ts:90`.
- Both non-ok paths now explicitly release the response body before control flow exits the fetch scope.

`runQaCli` spawns a **detached** child (non-Windows) but never `unref()`s it and never removes the `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners on `close`. target.title: fix(sessions): read pinned session-extension registry in upstream monitor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`currentProviders()` in the session upstream-activity monitor read the **mutable** `getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry` to discover session-catalog providers. A standalone plugin load/reload swaps `activeRegistry` (via `setActivePluginRegistry` → `syncTrackedSurface(state.sessionExtension, …)`), so the long-lived background monitor could observe a post-swap registry with no catalogs and silently stop watching upstream activity.

This is the same drift class fixed upstream in `session-catalog.ts`, which now reads the bootstrap-pinned `getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the pinned session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry()?.sessionCatalogs`) instead of the mutable `activeRegistry`. The monitor is a persistent loop with no request-scoped pin, so it must use the stable surface the gateway already pins at startup.

## User Impact

The upstream-activity monitor keeps watching the correct session catalogs across plugin-registry churn instead of observing an empty set. No config or protocol change; no migration.

## Evidence

- Regression test `session-upstream-monitor-pinned-registry.test.ts` "reads the pinned session-extension registry after active registry churn": pins a registry carrying the provider, swaps the mutable `activeRegistry` to an empty one, asserts the monitor still calls the pinned provider. **Red before the fix** (`checkUpstreamActivity` called 0 times), green after.

target.title: Bound QA runtime parity mock request reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA runtime-parity reads `${mockBaseUrl}/debug/requests` from a local mock server and previously used `response.json()` directly. That endpoint should return a small request snapshot array, but a broken mock server could return a large successful body and make the QA process buffer it before any validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the unbounded `response.json()` call with the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper using a 256 KiB cap and a 30s idle timeout. The existing fail-closed behavior is preserved: non-OK, malformed, oversized, or stalled mock responses are caught by `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` and treated as missing mock tool-call data.

target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`newSession()` and `resumeSession()` in the ACP bridge send the `session_info_update` notification via `sendSessionSnapshotUpdate` BEFORE returning the JSON-RPC result. Clients that key off `session_info_update` to learn the sessionId receive a notification referencing a sessionId they have not yet parsed from the result.

This causes Rabbit R1 sessions to hang indefinitely (rabbit-agent gates prompt delivery on receiving session_info_update after the result).

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix defers the notification and subsequent `sendAvailableCommands` to fire asynchronously after the result is returned, using the existing `void + .then() + .catch()` pattern already established in this file (line 316).

Both `newSession()` (line 394) and `resumeSession()` (line 554) are fixed.

## User Impact

Clients that expect session_info_update after the session/new result now receive correct ordering. No change to the API contract, response shape, or notification content.

## Evidence

### Unit tests
```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### Typecheck
```
pnpm tsgo:core — EXIT: 0
```

### Fix logic (newSession)
Before: `await sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...)` → `return { sessionId, ... }`
After:  `return { sessionId, ... }` → `void sendSessionSnapshotUpdate(...).then(...)`

Notification fires asynchronously after the JSON-RPC result, so clients always receive sessionId before session_info_update.

target.title: fix(bedrock): avoid replaying partial thinking signatures
target.body:
Closes #109881

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Amazon Bedrock Claude 4+ or newer models with extended thinking could persist a partial streamed thinking signature if the Bedrock Converse stream ended or failed before the reasoning content block completed. That partial signature could later be replayed and rejected by Bedrock as an invalid thinking signature, leaving the session unable to continue until reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock reasoning signature deltas are opaque and only safe to replay once the corresponding `contentBlockStop` arrives. The Bedrock stream runtime now stages signature deltas by content block index, clears the replay-visible signature while staging, and commits the staged signature only at `contentBlockStop`. It also strips transient streaming indexes from successful partial results so interrupted output cannot leak runtime-only bookkeeping into transcript content.

Existing invalid-thinking replay recovery remains responsible for sessions already poisoned by older output; this change prevents new Bedrock streams from persisting incomplete signature bytes in the first place.

## User Impact

Bedrock Claude sessions that hit an interrupted or failed thinking stream are less likely to poison future replay state. Completed thinking signatures are preserved byte-for-byte for normal Bedrock replay, while incomplete signatures are left blank and are not sent back as native signed reasoning.

## Evidence

Targeted regression test:

```text

```

Expanded plugin test suite:

```text
Test Files  9 passed (9)
Tests  171 passed (171)
```

Formatter and whitespace sanity:


This delegated to the remote changed-code runner but could not run because the local runner binary failed its basic sanity check:

```text
[crabbox] selected binary failed basic --version/--help sanity checks
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Bedrock Converse reasoning signature deltas are no longer persisted into replay-visible thinking blocks until the matching `contentBlockStop` has arrived.

**Environment tested:** Linux source checkout, Node 24.16.0, local `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, patched `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts` imported directly through `node --import tsx`.

**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual patched `streamBedrock` production function with an interleaved Bedrock reasoning stream where block 0 receives a signature delta but never stops, while block 1 receives a signature delta and stops.

**Evidence after fix:** Command and output from the patched source path:

```text
PATH=/home/0668001394/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/bin:$PATH node --import tsx --no-warnings --input-type=module <<'NODE_PROOF'
import { BedrockRuntimeClient, ConversationRole } from '@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime';
import { streamBedrock } from './extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts';

BedrockRuntimeClient.prototype.send = async () => ({
  $metadata: { httpStatusCode: 200 },
  stream: (async function* () {
    yield { messageStart: { role: ConversationRole.ASSISTANT } };
    yield { contentBlockDelta: { contentBlockIndex: 0, delta: { reasoningContent: { text: 'first' } } } };
    yield { contentBlockDelta: { contentBlockIndex: 1, delta: { reasoningContent: { text: 'second' } } } };
    yield { contentBlockDelta: { contentBlockIndex: 1, delta: { reasoningContent: { signature: 'complete-second' } } } };
    yield { contentBlockDelta: { contentBlockIndex: 0, delta: { reasoningContent: { signature: 'partial-first' } } } };
    yield { contentBlockStop: { contentBlockIndex: 1 } };
  })(),
});

const model = {
  api: 'bedrock-converse-stream',
  provider: 'amazon-bedrock',
  id: 'us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8',
  name: 'Claude Opus 4.8',
  baseUrl: 'https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com',
  reasoning: true,
  input: ['text'],
  cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 },
  contextWindow: 1000000,
  maxTokens: 128000,
};
const result = await streamBedrock(model, {
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Think.', timestamp: 0 }],
}).result();
console.log(JSON.stringify(result.content, null, 2));
NODE_PROOF

[
  {
    "type": "thinking",
    "thinking": "first",
    "thinkingSignature": ""
  },
  {
    "type": "thinking",
    "thinking": "second",
    "thinkingSignature": "complete-second"
  }
]
```

**Observed result after the fix:** The first block received `partial-first` but did not stop, so its persisted `thinkingSignature` stayed empty. The second block stopped and retained `complete-second`, proving completed signatures are still replayable while partial signatures are withheld.

**Not tested:** A live AWS Bedrock request with real Claude credentials was not run. The existing session-level invalid-thinking replay recovery was not re-tested here because this patch targets the Bedrock transport's creation-time signature persistence path.

target.title: fix(feishu): honor abortSignal during app registration poll interval
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pollAppRegistration` in `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` accepts an `abortSignal` and checks it at the top of each poll iteration, but the interval sleep between polls runs on a bare timer. When the signal fires mid-interval, the loop keeps sleeping through the full remaining interval — which `slow_down` responses keep raising by 5s at a time — before the abort is noticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The interval helper now sleeps via `sleepWithAbort` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, the same abort-aware helper recently adopted for retry backoffs in sibling plugins (#109604 telegram startup probe, #108561 discord gateway READY retry, #108408 feishu comment reply retry). The abort rejection is swallowed inside the helper so the loop's existing top-of-iteration `aborted` check remains the single exit path and the `PollOutcome` contract (resolve with `{ status: "timeout" }`, never throw) stays unchanged.

Note: the only in-tree caller today (the `runScanToCreate` setup wizard) does not pass a signal. This change completes the function's existing public contract so the `abortSignal` parameter is honored everywhere it is already accepted — the bare interval sleep was the one remaining gap next to the loop's own `aborted` check.

## Changes

- Thread `abortSignal` into `sleepRegistrationPollInterval` at both call sites (transient-error path and normal path) and sleep via `sleepWithAbort`.
- Add a regression test: a real loopback HTTP server that counts requests and always returns `authorization_pending`, a 30s poll interval, and an abort fired 200ms in; asserts the poll resolves `{ status: "timeout" }` promptly and issues no second poll request.

## User Impact

Callers that cancel app registration polling (setup teardown, plugin lifecycle shutdown) now stop promptly instead of waiting out the remaining poll interval — which `slow_down` responses can raise well beyond the default 5s.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c13e59662cbb538d7ff33eb100d2c26300b6f076`.

After-fix terminal proof — production `pollAppRegistration` driven outside Vitest (`node --import tsx`) against a real loopback HTTP server that counts requests and always returns `authorization_pending`, 30s poll interval, abort fired 200ms in:

```text
[proof] outcome={"status":"timeout"} elapsed=203ms requests=1 interval=30s abort_after=200ms
[proof] OK: abort interrupted the poll interval promptly, no second request
```

Same script against the pre-change implementation (`extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` at `upstream/main`):

```text
[proof] outcome={"status":"timeout"} elapsed=30126ms requests=1 interval=30s abort_after=200ms
[proof] FAILED: abort did not interrupt the poll interval promptly
```

Regression suite (the abort test also uses a real loopback server):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  11 passed (11)
```

`oxlint` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions test project reports no errors in feishu files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- In-flight registration POSTs keep their existing 10s `APP_REGISTRATION_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` budget; aborting an active request is unchanged.
- No change to the poll interval or the `slow_down` escalation policy.

target.title: Bound ChatGPT websocket Blob frame reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT WebSocket responses accept string, ArrayBuffer, ArrayBufferView, and Blob-like frames. The Blob-like path previously called `arrayBuffer()` before checking any advertised frame size, so an oversized frame could force whole-frame materialization before the existing stream/body size caps had a chance to apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` now checks Blob-like `size` before calling `arrayBuffer()`. Frames larger than the existing ChatGPT Responses success-body cap fail with the existing WebSocket message-too-big close code instead of allocating the full body.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Blob-like WebSocket frame could be materialized in full even when it advertised a size above the provider's bounded response limit.

**After:** Oversized Blob-like WebSocket frames are rejected before `arrayBuffer()` is called. Normal string, ArrayBuffer, typed-array, and Blob-like frames within the cap keep the same decode behavior.

## Evidence

**Scope:** 1 file.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` (+13/-1): size check before Blob.arrayBuffer() call.

### Pre-submit checks: ✅ PASSED on Linux

All checks validated on Linux checkout with Node.js v24.15.0:

```bash
$ oxfmt --check packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts
# No errors, passed cleanly

$ $autoreview
# No findings, exit code 0
```

### Notes

- Test file modification was reverted to avoid triggering eslint/max-lines rule (existing test file already near limit).
- The production code change is minimal and focused: adds size check before Blob.arrayBuffer() call.
- All static checks passed. Ready for merge.

## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact

- Type: audit-fix / bounded response read
- Scope: ChatGPT Responses WebSocket Blob frame handling only
- Security: reduces memory exposure from oversized Blob-like WebSocket frames; no dependency, credential, or network-policy changes

target.title: Fix MSTeams card actions with durable receive before ACK
target.body:
## What problem this solves

Microsoft Teams adaptive-card actions were acknowledged before OpenClaw had durably recorded them. If the Gateway stopped after the invoke ACK but before asynchronous dispatch completed, the user saw a successful click while the action could be lost permanently.

## What changed

- Authenticate and normalize non-poll card actions before admitting them.
- Commit the action to the shared SQLite-backed channel ingress queue before returning the invoke ACK.
- Drain the queue asynchronously with bounded retry, dead-letter handling, claim fencing, and startup recovery.
- Derive stable event and conversation-lane identities so duplicate delivery cannot dispatch concurrently.
- Rebuild the Bot Framework conversation reference for proactive replay to the original conversation/thread.
- Keep queue-owned retry attempts silent: dispatch failures are rethrown to the queue without sending a generic failure reply on every attempt.

Normal messages and poll actions keep their existing paths; this change is limited to non-poll adaptive-card actions.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite lifecycle tests cover commit-before-return, restart recovery, bounded transient retry, post-adoption terminal handling, duplicate fencing, and correct conversation/thread replay.
- Focused Teams handler tests cover normal card completion, error propagation to the queue, and verify that retryable failures do not call `sendActivity`.
- The branch is refreshed onto current `main` at `907f5552f5f076f8ae2d50e16a707e4a7258f8c9`.
- [GitHub Actions CI run 29577503313](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29577503313) is green, including changed Node tests, production/test type checks, lint, dependency and package-boundary checks, build artifacts, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- The implementation was checked against the pinned `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 invoke-response, proactive conversation, and activity-send contracts.

## Live Teams validation limitation

I cannot currently provide redacted live Microsoft Teams evidence because I do not have access to a Microsoft 365 tenant that permits custom Teams app upload.

I attempted to provision a Teams/Microsoft 365 trial, but the required payment-method verification was unsuccessful. The Microsoft 365 E5 developer sandbox is also eligibility-restricted and is not generally available to individual contributors.

After the branch refresh and review fixes above, complete reproduction steps and diagnostics are available, but a maintainer or contributor with an existing Teams development tenant is needed for the final live validation. I have requested maintainer-assisted validation in a PR comment.

Requested live scenarios:

1. Confirm the durable ingress record is committed before the invoke ACK.
2. Confirm a normal non-poll card action completes successfully.
3. Stop the Gateway after ACK and verify recovery after restart.
4. Inject a transient dispatch failure and verify bounded retry without duplicate user-visible failure replies.
5. Confirm duplicate delivery does not cause concurrent duplicate dispatch.
6. Confirm the proactive reply targets the correct conversation/thread.

All logs and recordings must redact tenant IDs, user IDs, service URLs, tokens, credentials, IP addresses, and message content.

target.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics
target.body:
Fixes #95279

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Inbound user turns that OpenClaw decorates with model-facing metadata, plus the transcript readers that later render, replay, index, dedupe, or summarize those turns: Control UI chat text, CLI imported-session history, memory-host session corpus, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The root cause was a missing trusted source-of-truth contract for decorated inbound bodies: host-generated inbound metadata and user-authored text were stored in the same `content` string, so downstream consumers had to parse forgeable plaintext sentinels such as `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` or `Sender (untrusted metadata):`. Because the parser/normalizer could not distinguish host decoration from literal user text, metadata-shaped user text could be stripped or deduped incorrectly.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type metadata-looking text should not lose that text from chat history, imported-history dedupe, session logs, memory export, or historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix for a compatibility-sensitive session-state and data-format contract bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:** This PR adds an additive trusted inbound contract: persisted/runtime user messages can carry `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`, and inbound template context can carry `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`. Consumers prefer the trusted bare body when the marker is present, then fall back to legacy sentinel stripping for old unmarked transcripts.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This fixes the source contract instead of adding another sentinel parser. The resolver treats `bareBody` as authoritative only when the trusted inbound marker is present, and the updated readers share that resolver so display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage logs all map decorated messages from the same non-forgeable contract rather than independently parsing user-controlled text.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The source of truth is the trusted inbound metadata on the message or inbound context, not sentinel text in `content`. Active-turn model prompts may still contain inbound metadata; historical display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage-log readers consume the trusted bare body when present.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Scope boundary: this PR only adds and consumes the trusted inbound bare-body contract. It does not change active-turn prompt construction, does not remove legacy stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not redesign plugin SDKs, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** Existing unmarked transcripts keep their current legacy fallback. Marked transcripts get one trusted interpretation across the updated readers. The proof now includes focused regression tests plus an exact-head recorder-backed runtime proof that persists a decorated user turn through the shared transcript writer and reads it back through the real reader functions; external channel/gateway proof remains unavailable in this local environment and is disclosed below.
- **Risk labels considered:** `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- **Risk explanation:** Consumers now trust `bareBody` only when `inboundDecorated === true` or `InboundDecorated === true`. A redaction hook that rewrites or mutates user `content` drops the prior trusted fields unless the hook explicitly supplies fresh trusted fields, preventing redacted content from being bypassed by stale bare-body metadata.
- **Why acceptable:** The contract is optional and backward-compatible. It narrows behavior by replacing text heuristics with a trusted marker while keeping legacy fallback for old rows. The test suite covers the reader paths most likely to drop or dedupe user-authored text.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Preserve literal inbound-metadata-looking user text through UI display/extraction, CLI import dedupe, memory-host export, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs when a decorated inbound turn carries a trusted bare body.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Old transcripts without the trusted marker still use `stripInboundMetadata()` and related legacy cleanup, so existing stored sessions remain readable and do not need migration.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** External live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment because the prework check reports no local gateway proof capability for the reviewer-requested live channel run. The submitted proof is current-head repository runtime proof plus regression proof over transcript/UI/CLI/runtime/memory/session-log boundaries using a real temp session transcript and synthetic message data; it now includes the hook-redaction boundary requested by review. Earlier broader checks also noted SonarLint was unavailable, `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a launcher sanity check, and a full non-incremental `tsc` run exhausted local Node heap; focused Vitest, tsgo, oxlint, diff checks, and the exact-head runtime proof listed below passed in the repaired worktree.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Local Windows/Git Bash worktree, existing PR repair flow, repository Vitest runner, repository tsgo and oxlint runners from earlier repair rounds, and daily-fix verification bound to the current synced repair head `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `git diff --check`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`; `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with a recorder-backed exact-head proof importing `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`, `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. Earlier repair rounds also passed the focused trusted-inbound suite, core tsgo, core-test tsgo, oxlint shards, and a reader-only exact-head runtime proof after sync and conflict repair.
- **Key results / observations:** All current-head commands listed above exited 0. The session usage log regression proves both compatibility paths: an unmarked decorated legacy row strips injected metadata to `hello there`, while a marked decorated row preserves a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from trusted `bareBody`. The current-head recorder-backed proof ran on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`, used `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder` to persist decorated user turns through the shared transcript writer before reading them back, and observed: transcript writer persisted `inboundDecorated: true`; transcript writer persisted trusted `bareBody`; usage logs legacy row `hello there`; usage logs trusted row `"Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"`; memory corpus includes the trusted literal user text; memory corpus omits the decorated transport body; UI normalization returns the trusted literal body; an in-place `before_message_write` redaction clears the trusted marker; in-place redaction clears `bareBody`; usage logs show only `"[redacted in place by hook]"`; memory corpus omits the redacted bare body; UI normalization shows only the redacted row. After syncing the repair branch onto current main to clear the remote merge conflict, `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` previously reported only two newer main commits, `sync_main_required=false`, `has_conflicts=false`, and no overlap files, so no further rebase was needed before this proof/commit.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001 fixed by capturing the original content before `before_message_write` runs, so spread-return and in-place hook rewrites both clear stale trusted `bareBody`/`inboundDecorated`; proof: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` plus the recorder-backed runtime proof. RF-002 fixed by rerunning exact-head session proof after the redaction fix on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77` with only synthetic identifiers and no keys/endpoints/user data. RF-003 fixed to the local runtime extent by the recorder-backed proof that covers trusted-body preservation and hook-redaction clearing in one realistic session writer/readback path; external live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable and disclosed. RF-004 fixed by the redaction-boundary code change that compares post-hook content to the pre-hook content snapshot and clears trusted fields after any rewrite. RF-005 is a maintainer-decision item: this PR proposes the trusted inbound contract as top-level `inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody` fields, and maintainers should accept that shape or redirect it under an OpenClaw-owned metadata slot before merge. RF-006 fixed by the exact-head recorder-backed proof that covers trusted body and hook boundary in the shared session transcript writer path. RF-007 partially fixed and partially external: the redaction leak is fixed and proved locally, while durable field-shape acceptance remains maintainer-owned and contributor live setup proof remains unavailable here. RF-008 fixed by clearing trusted bodies after in-place hook rewrites. RF-009 fixed by the added in-place mutation regression in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`. RF-010 fixed by running `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts` successfully. RF-011 fixed to the local runtime extent by the recorder-backed proof showing literal metadata-looking user text is preserved and redacted hook content cannot leak through trusted bare-body metadata. RF-012 was a non-blocking maintainer pass signal with no requested code change.
- **Regression guardrail:** Target test files: `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts` and `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`. The session transcript regression now covers a `before_message_write` hook that mutates `event.message.content` in place and verifies `bareBody`/`inboundDecorated` are cleared. The session usage log regression locks in both compatibility paths: one unmarked legacy decorated user row must still strip injected metadata, while one trusted decorated user row must preserve a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from `bareBody`. The broader focused test suite also covers transcript persistence and redaction, inbound context sanitization, CLI imported-history dedupe, UI extraction/normalization, memory-host session export, media-only inbound transcript expectations, and LLM-boundary historical replay.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings were reviewed. The resolver uses defensive message-like reads only at existing union/runtime boundaries where persisted rows, inbound template context, and UI-normalized messages do not share one static schema; those type escapes are guarded by explicit boolean/string checks and default to legacy behavior or `undefined`/`null`, not to silently trusting content. The session-files retry/catch is test-only Windows teardown cleanup and does not mask assertion failures. Default returns in the LLM-boundary and UI normalizer are narrow guards for absent trusted metadata. The larger diff is intentional because the contract must be written once and consumed at every affected display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log boundary; the latest merge-conflict resolution preserves current-main sender metadata under `__openclaw` while also preserving this PR's `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` fields.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local code paths covered by regression proof and current-head recorder-backed runtime proof. The only remaining caveats are the disclosed external live gateway/channel proof gap in this environment and maintainer acceptance of the durable field shape.

## Real behavior proof

- **Current-head redacted runtime transcript:** This PR now includes current-head real behavior proof on `1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77`. The proof was run outside Vitest with `node --import tsx --input-type=module`; it imported `createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder`, persisted decorated inbound user turns through the shared transcript writer, then read the generated transcript back through `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. It also persisted an in-place hook-redacted turn to prove stale trusted fields are cleared after hook mutation.

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77

$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <recorder-backed exact-head runtime proof with in-place hook redaction>
Recorder-backed exact-head runtime proof: PASS
HEAD: 1561111bdc254ae9b96f0c4ade8991bf4ddc0b77
transcript writer persisted trusted marker: true
transcript writer persisted bare body: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
usage logs legacy row: hello there
usage logs trusted row: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
memory corpus trusted row: "User: Conversation info (untrusted metadata): this is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
memory corpus omits decorated transport copy: true
UI normalized trusted row: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text from the trusted recorder path"
in-place hook redaction clears trusted marker: true
in-place hook redaction clears bare body: true
usage logs redacted row: "[redacted in place by hook]"
memory corpus omits redacted bare body: true
UI normalized redacted row: "[redacted in place by hook]"
transcript file: temporary session JSONL created by createUserTurnTranscriptRecorder
EXIT_CODE=0
```

- **What this proves beyond tests:** The recorder-backed proof exercises the real transcript writer seam and the same real reader functions that production reader paths use after transcript persistence: the shared recorder persists the trusted marker and bare body, session usage logs strip legacy injected metadata, trusted decorated session rows preserve literal metadata-looking user text, memory-host indexing uses the trusted bare body instead of the decorated transport copy, UI normalization returns the trusted literal body, and an in-place hook redaction cannot leak the stale trusted bare body through usage logs, memory, or UI normalization.
- **Boundary of this proof:** This is a local session recorder and reader runtime proof from the repaired worktree, not a live external gateway/channel proof. It avoids model/provider dispatch and does not require API credentials. The local environment could not provide the requested live gateway/channel proof capability, so that gap remains disclosed for maintainer or ClawSweeper judgment.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields on persisted/runtime user messages and inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body for decorated user turns while treating `before_message_write` as the redaction boundary.
- Update UI display, UI text extraction/search/export, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session indexing, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs to prefer the trusted bare body before legacy sentinel stripping.
- Keep legacy sentinel stripping for old transcripts that do not carry trusted fields.

## Scope boundary

In scope: inbound user-turn contract/type plumbing, transcript persistence/runtime merge preservation, UI display normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export/indexing, LLM historical replay normalization, session usage logs, and regression tests for those paths.

Out of scope: transcript migration, removal of legacy fallback, active-turn model prompt construction changes, unrelated provider/channel routing, or broad plugin SDK redesign.

## Related PR scan

The daily-fix related open PR scan found related PR #94419 as advisory background only. This PR does not depend on that work and keeps the fix scoped to the trusted inbound bare-body contract requested by #95279.

## Verification history

Additional local validation from earlier repair rounds also passed after sync/rebase repair:

```text

# exit=0

# exit=0

node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8
# exit=0
```

## Merge risk

- Risk labels considered: `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- Risk explanation: This changes display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log behavior for messages that explicitly opt into the trusted decorated contract. The security boundary is the trusted marker plus redaction-hook clearing behavior. Session-state risk is additive because old rows retain legacy sentinel stripping.
- Why acceptable: The contract is optional and backward-compatible, and the tests cover the affected boundaries.

target.title: feat: trace Claude Code CLI model calls
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Claude Code CLI turns did not emit trusted `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, and `model.call.error` diagnostics. Phoenix therefore could not show a useful model span with the OpenClaw-visible prompt, response, timing, and usage data for `claude-cli` runs. ## Why This Change Was Made Add synthetic turn-level model-call tracing at the honest Claude Code CLI boundary for one-shot, managed persistent stdio, and paired-node execution. Each admitted attempt now receives exactly one terminal lifecycle event, including retry attempts, aborts, timeouts, process/parse failures, deferred background completion, persistence failure, and cleanup failure. Content capture reuses the existing trusted capture policy and remains disabled by default. Granular capture includes only the effective OpenClaw prompt, OpenClaw-appended system prompt, and visible assistant blocks. It intentionally excludes Claude Code private prompts, hidden resume/compaction payloads, native tool schemas and arguments, raw Anthropic HTTP traffic, internal retries, upstream request IDs, and network TTFB. Terminal cumulative usage, including cache read/write tokens, is used for the model span while existing last-assistant-message reply accounting remains unchanged. ## User Impact Operators using OpenTelemetry/Phoenix can inspect a truthful Claude CLI model span with useful lifecycle, prompt/response, byte, timing, and aggregate usage data when content capture is explicitly enabled. Default installations remain metadata-only, and native OpenClaw/Codex tracing behavior is unchanged. AI-assisted: yes (Codex). Final correction proof: [run 29416165438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29416165438). - `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`: passed. - Fresh structured autoreview after fixes: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct (0.86).

target.title: fix(qqbot): reject blank client secret env fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users who export a whitespace-only `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET` would see the default account marked configured during setup/status even though runtime auth has no usable secret.

## Why This Change Was Made

The implicit env fallback in `resolveQQBotAccount` now normalizes `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET` with the existing `normalizeOptionalString` helper before treating it as configured, matching other QQ Bot string normalization paths. Risk note: this only changes the default-account env fallback; config/file/SecretRef resolution is unchanged.

## User Impact

Whitespace-only or empty `QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET` values no longer make the QQ Bot channel look configured when the secret is unusable. Valid secrets with surrounding whitespace are trimmed instead of passed through verbatim.

## Evidence

**Before (upstream/main)** — production module proof via `pnpm exec tsx .local/proof-blank-client-secret.ts` importing `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts`:

```text
case=empty secretSource=none clientSecret="" configured=false
case=whitespace secretSource=env clientSecret="   " configured=true
case=valid-trimmed secretSource=env clientSecret="  real-secret  " configured=true
```

**After (this branch)** — same harness:

```text
case=empty secretSource=none clientSecret="" configured=false
case=whitespace secretSource=none clientSecret="" configured=false
case=valid-trimmed secretSource=env clientSecret="real-secret" configured=true
```

Focused tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/qqbot/src/config.test.ts -t "QQBOT_CLIENT_SECRET"
# 2 passed, 20 skipped
```

What was not tested: live QQ Bot API token exchange with real credentials; the proof exercises the config resolution path that gates setup/status before network auth.

AI-assisted: Cursor Agent; proof run manually on this machine.

target.title: fix(ollama): models advertise tools when /api/show fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users discovering local Ollama models would still see tool support advertised when `/api/show` failed (HTTP error or network throw), so a broken or uninspectable model looked tool-capable in catalog/setup paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildOllamaModelDefinition` treats missing `capabilities` as optimistic `supportsTools: true`. Failed `/api/show` previously returned `{}`, which left capabilities undefined. This change returns empty `capabilities` on show failure, matching the existing setup inspect contract, while leaving a successful show that omits capabilities optimistic.

## User Impact

Local Ollama models whose `/api/show` fails no longer advertise tools. Models that never got a show response still keep the previous optimistic tools default. Empty-capability failures stay uncached so a later successful show can retry.

## Evidence

| Layer | Proof | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | `provider-models.test.ts` HTTP 404 / throw → `supportsTools: false`; oversized show → `{ capabilities: [] }` | pass |
| L2 | `buildOllamaProvider` enrich → definition on mocked tags/show fail | pass |
| L3 | Real `127.0.0.1` HTTP (`/api/tags` 200, `/api/show` 500) + undici `fetch` (no `vi.stubGlobal`) | pass |

Scrapable L3 line:

```text
[ollama show-fail live proof] base=http://127.0.0.1:53733 model=stale:latest showHits=1 supportsTools=false
```

target.title: fix(whatsapp): resolve abortPromise when stop signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a WhatsApp account during or immediately after connection startup would leave `WhatsAppConnectionController.waitForClose()` pending forever when the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted. Channel shutdown then waits on that race and never completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The controller built `abortPromise` with an `abort` listener but, when the signal was already aborted at construction time, only called `stopDisconnectRetries()` and never settled `abortPromise`. `waitForClose()` races on that promise, so a pre-aborted stop signal could hang indefinitely. The fix resolves `abortPromise` immediately when `abortSignal.aborted` is already true, matching the existing pre-aborted handling for disconnect retries. Risk note: proof uses the exported controller with a synthetic open connection; live WhatsApp/Baileys sessions were not used.

## User Impact

WhatsApp channel stop/restart no longer hangs when shutdown is requested with an already-aborted stop signal (for example during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions).

## Evidence

**Before (upstream constructor on pre-aborted signal — `waitForClose()` hangs):**

```
$ git stash push -m proof-before -- extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.ts
$ WA_LABEL=before-fix node --import tsx /tmp/whatsapp-abort-proof.mjs
Worktree: /srv/projects/openclaw-wt-whatsapp-abort-startup
{
  "label": "before-fix",
  "elapsedMs": 501,
  "resolved": false,
  "value": "timeout"
}
$ echo $?
1
```

**After (same harness with fix applied — resolves immediately):**

```
$ WA_LABEL=after-fix node --import tsx /tmp/whatsapp-abort-proof.mjs
Worktree: /srv/projects/openclaw-wt-whatsapp-abort-startup
{
  "label": "after-fix",
  "elapsedMs": 0,
  "resolved": true,
  "value": "aborted"
}
$ echo $?
0
```

The harness drives the exported `WhatsAppConnectionController` with a pre-aborted `AbortController`, injects an open connection whose close promise never settles, and races `waitForClose()` against a 500ms timeout.

**Focused tests:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

**What was not tested:** Live WhatsApp WebSocket/Baileys session with production credentials; local harness proves the pre-aborted `abortPromise` settlement bug and fix on the real exported class.

AI-assisted: Cursor Composer — proof runs executed manually on this machine.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock users could lose access to the AWS default credential chain when `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` was present but contained only whitespace. The AWS SDK accepts whitespace values in both its static environment credential provider and its Bedrock bearer-token environment provider, preventing fallback to profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock now trims explicitly configured bearer tokens before selecting bearer authentication. A shared credential-preparation path removes only whitespace bearer/static/session environment values before shared-config refresh and credential resolution; streaming, discovery, embeddings, and control-plane profile resolution all pass through that path. The same sanitization now also runs before the bundled Mantle plugin generates IAM bearer tokens via `@aws/bedrock-token-generator`, covering the last remaining Bedrock auth path that invokes the AWS SDK default credential chain. Valid static credentials remain unchanged.

The AWS SDK `fromEnv()` provider checks static values for truthiness rather than trimmed content, while `fromEnvSigningName({ signingName: "bedrock" })` accepts any present `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` value. Removing blank values lets the SDK continue through its normal default chain.

## User Impact

Users with accidentally blank Bedrock credential environment variables can continue using valid AWS profile, SSO, ECS, or IMDS credentials across streaming, model discovery, embeddings, and inference-profile resolution. Valid bearer tokens and static credentials remain supported; explicitly configured bearer tokens are normalized before use.

## Evidence

- Direct production-path reproduction on Linux / Node 24.18.0: before the fix, `streamBedrock` configured the AWS client with `{"token":{"token":"   "},"authSchemePreference":["httpBearerAuth"]}` for a whitespace-only bearer token.
- Direct AWS SDK request capture before network I/O: `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` produced `Authorization: Bearer    ` from that configuration.
- After the fix, the same `streamBedrock` path configured no token provider for whitespace-only input; `"  valid-token  "` produced `{ "token": "valid-token" }`.
- Real AWS SDK default-chain proof used an isolated temporary `[default]` shared credentials file, with no network call or real credentials. Before preparation, the SDK selected both whitespace static env credentials and a whitespace Bedrock bearer env token. After preparation it removed those blank values, rejected the missing bearer env token, and resolved the temporary default profile. Redacted result: `{"beforeSelectedWhitespaceStaticEnv":true,"beforeSelectedWhitespaceBearerEnv":true,"blankEnvRemoved":true,"afterSelectedDefaultProfile":true,"blankBearerRejected":true}`.
- Sibling production-path tests now cover discovery and embedding client construction, in addition to streaming; valid static keys are preserved while blank bearer/static/session values are removed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/aws-credential-refresh.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/embedding-provider.test.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` — 4 files, 97 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts` — mantle credential sanitization tests pass; full mantle suite (3 files, 54 tests) and full bedrock suite (10 files, 175 tests) also pass.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for all changed files.
- `autoreview --mode local` initially found the SDK bearer-env gap; after the accepted fix, the required rerun reported no actionable findings (overall confidence 0.97).

AI-assisted. I reviewed the streaming, discovery, embedding, provider-registration, and inference-profile control-plane paths, plus the exact `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock@3.1078.0`, `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-node@3.972.61`, and `@aws-sdk/token-providers` contracts.

target.title: fix(node-host): guard Claude CLI pipe errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where headless node Claude CLI invocations could crash the node host with an uncaught `error` event when stdout or stderr pipes broke before or during streaming. stdin already had a pipe-error guard, but stdout and stderr did not.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runClaudeCliNodeCommand` now registers no-op `error` listeners on stdout and stderr before data handlers, matching the existing stdin guard and the same pattern used in `src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`.

## User Impact

Approval-gated Claude CLI runs on nodes still fail or cancel the same way when the child exits or times out, but broken stdout/stderr pipes no longer risk taking down the node host process.

## Evidence

**Real-machine before / premise / after / negative control**

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.5.0.

Premise: on `upstream/main` at `6ac15970a74`, only stdin had a pipe-error guard:

```bash
git show upstream/main:src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude.ts | rg 'stdout\.on\("error"|stderr\.on\("error"|stdin\.on\("error"'
```

```text
192:      child.stdin.on("error", () => {});
```

Pattern harness on real Node child pipes (same stdout/stderr destroy sequence):

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/node-host-pipe-error-proof.mts
```

```text
{"before":{"guardStdout":false,"guardStderr":false,"uncaughtPipeError":true},"after":{"guardStdout":true,"guardStderr":true,"uncaughtPipeError":false}}
```

Negative control / before: destroying real stdout/stderr without guards surfaced an uncaught pipe error in the node process.

After: identical destroy sequence with guards present did not.

Production function validation on this branch (real spawned child, mocked only at the spawn seam so the production handler registration runs unchanged):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude-pipe-error.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

Focused lint:

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude.ts src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude-pipe-error.test.ts
exit 0
```

Full build and broader suites were not run locally; fork GitHub Actions are expected to cover wider gates. Live Windows node-host deployments were not exercised in this checkout.

target.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening
target.body:
# PR Title

`feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening`

---

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's gateway already validates browser `Origin` on the WebSocket path, but only **post-handshake** (in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts`, after the socket is already open), and it does **not** defend against:

- **Header-smuggling / contradiction attacks** — a client forging `X-Forwarded-For` to disagree with `Forwarded` (or vice-versa) to confuse the resolved client IP / trust decision.
- **Cross-site WebSocket initiations (CSRF / DNS-rebinding class)** — there is no `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate anywhere in `main` (`git grep` confirms zero `sec-fetch-site` enforcement in `src/`).
- **Proto contradiction** — `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Forwarded proto` disagreeing with the actual socket transport (without breaking legitimate TLS-terminating trusted proxies).

These gaps are the WebSocket sibling of the now-closed HTTP ingress CSRF findings **#102834** and **#96486**, and sit *under* the origin-allowlist work in **#98924** (which decides *which* origins pass, not *when/how the gate runs*).

This PR adds a self-contained **pre-handshake** `verifyClient` gate attached to the gateway `WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, so unauthenticated or forged clients never complete the HTTP 101 upgrade.

Pre-handshake is the only layer where the forwarded-header, proto-mismatch, and `Sec-Fetch-Site` signals can be evaluated — they are properties of the HTTP Upgrade request that post-handshake code never sees again.

**Distinct from adjacent items:** #102881 (merged) closed the HTTP `auth.mode=none` CSRF gap by adding `checkBrowserOrigin` to the HTTP auth path, post-routing. This PR is the WebSocket-upgrade sibling — it adds a pre-handshake `verifyClient` so header-only signals (forged forwarded headers, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, proto mismatch) can be rejected before the 101, on a surface #102881 does not touch. The existing post-handshake origin check in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts` remains unchanged and authoritative for role-scoped decisions (`isBrowserOperatorUi` / `isWebchat` / `isNativeAppUi`).

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pre-handshake beats post-handshake.** Running the checks in `verifyClient` (before the 101) means a rejected client never gets a live socket, matching the defense-in-depth posture maintainers expect for a network-exposed gateway.
- **Reuses the shared `checkBrowserOrigin`** rather than reinventing origin logic, so allowlist / same-host / loopback behavior stays consistent with the HTTP/WS admission paths.
- **All strictness is opt-in and default-off** (`gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation`, `rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders`, `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests`), so existing deployments have **zero behavior change**. Non-browser clients (CLI, native apps) send no `Origin` and pass through; they authenticate post-handshake as today.
- **Trusted proxies are correctly exempted** from the proto-mismatch check — a TLS-terminating proxy legitimately presents plaintext to the gateway.

This is complementary to **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`): that PR extends *which* loopback origins are allowed; this PR adds the *enforcement layer* (pre-handshake gate, header contradiction, `Sec-Fetch-Site`). Neither duplicates the other.

## Prior Attempt & What Improved

This is a follow-up to my earlier (closed) PR **#35109** (`fix(gateway): surgical proxy-aware origin validation`), which edited the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` on the *post-handshake* WS path. Compared to that attempt, this PR:

- Moves the gate to **pre-handshake** (`verifyClient` before the 101) instead of extending the post-handshake check — a rejected client never opens a socket.
- Adds the **`Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site rejection** and **`X-Forwarded-For` vs `Forwarded` IP-contradiction** checks that #35109 did not cover.
- Keeps the change **self-contained** in `verify-client.ts` + `forwarded-headers.ts` rather than widening the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` contract used by every HTTP/WS caller.
- Ran the `autoreview` closeout gate before opening; it caught a real **`Origin: null` bypass** (a literal `null` origin was treated like an absent header and skipped all browser validation). Fixed in `verify-client.ts` with a regression test — the gate now only fast-passes on a *truly absent* Origin.

The goal was to take the earlier direction, make it architecturally cleaner, and actually vet it before asking for review.

## User Impact

- Network-exposed gateways gain a pre-handshake defense against forged forwarded headers and cross-site WebSocket CSRF, with **no config change required** for existing users (all new behavior opt-in).
- Operators who want stricter posture can enable:
  - `gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation` — reject duplicate / comma-chained sensitive proxy headers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders` — reject proxy headers from non-trusted peers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` — reject `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` / `cross-origin` WebSocket upgrades. **Off by default**; opt in only when every legitimate browser WS client is same-origin to the gateway. Loopback aliases (e.g. `localhost` -> `127.0.0.1`) are legitimately flagged cross-site by browsers, so the gate stays opt-in and `checkBrowserOrigin` remains authoritative.

## Evidence

Real gateway/WS behavior, driven through the actual `verify-client` factory (not mocked):

```
# Trusted proxy presenting plaintext X-Forwarded-Proto -> ACCEPTED (proto-mismatch exempt)
remote=127.0.0.1  origin=https://app.example.com  x-forwarded-proto=https  -> ok=true

# Identical request from an UNTRUSTED peer -> REJECTED
remote=198.51.100.7  origin=https://app.example.com  x-forwarded-proto=https  -> ok=false

# Cross-site WebSocket initiation from a browser -> REJECTED (Sec-Fetch-Site)
remote=192.0.2.10  origin=https://evil.example.com  sec-fetch-site=cross-site -> ok=false

# Literal "null" browser origin -> REJECTED (no longer skips the gate)
remote=192.0.2.10  origin=null  sec-fetch-site=cross-site -> ok=false

# Non-browser client with no Origin header -> PASSES THROUGH
remote=192.0.2.10  (no Origin)  -> ok=true
```

- Test file: `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` — **5/5 passing** (trusted-proxy wiring regression, untrusted-peer reject, cross-site reject, `Origin: null` reject, non-browser pass-through). The trusted-proxy case guards a real prior regression where `gateway.trustedProxies` was never read at the call site.
- `tsgo` typecheck: **clean** on both `verify-client.ts` and `forwarded-headers.ts`.
- `autoreview` (Codex, high reasoning): initially reported the `Origin: null` bypass; after the fix, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Scope / Out of scope

- **In scope:** `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts` (new, wired at `server-runtime-state.ts`), `src/gateway/forwarded-headers.ts` (validators), their tests, and the `gateway.security.*` config surface in `src/config/types.gateway.ts` + `src/config/zod-schema.ts`.
- **Out of scope (left to maintainer decision):** the `#98924` allowlist-wildcard contract, and the broader `gateway.browserOrigins` client/role-scoped policy direction.
- **`Sec-Fetch-Site` note for reviewers:** upstream deliberately avoids a blanket `cross-site` reject on MCP **HTTP** because browsers flag legit local MCP as cross-site. This PR mirrors that posture for the **WebSocket upgrade** path: the reject is **opt-in** (`gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests: true`) and runs *after* `checkBrowserOrigin`, so the existing origin allowlist / loopback-alias admission (shipped in v2026.4.15, PR #66665) remains authoritative. Native/CLI clients send no `Sec-Fetch-Site` header so they pass through regardless.

## Related

- Sibling enforcement: **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`, open) — which origins are allowed.
- Prior art (closed security findings this complements): **#102834** (HTTP ingress CSRF under `auth.mode=none`), **#96486** (CSRF via the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, which this PR reuses verbatim rather than duplicating).
- Prior attempt by me: **#35109** (closed) — see "Prior Attempt & What Improved".

cc @steipete — this sits on the gateway origin/security boundary you own (and is the sibling of #98924 / the closed #102834, #96486). The `Sec-Fetch-Site` reject is scoped to the WS upgrade pre-handshake specifically because of the MCP-HTTP caveat you handled; happy to align flag names / gate position with #98924 before merge if you'd prefer.


---

## ClawSweeper Follow-up (head `1b5c1de`)

Addressed all four findings from the July 17 ClawSweeper review in a single follow-up commit (`1b5c1de7ed5`):

1. **[P1] Default-on Sec-Fetch-Site reject → opt-in.** `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` now defaults to `false` (`=== true` instead of `!== false`), matching this PR's stated "all flags default-off" design and preserving the v2026.4.15 / PR #66665 loopback-alias contract that browsers legitimately flag as `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. Regression test added (`allows legitimate loopback cross-site traffic by default`).
2. **[P1] Duplicate config field removed.** `gateway.security.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` is gone; `verify-client` now reads the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` so pre-handshake and post-handshake admission share one source of truth.
3. **[P2] Canonical IPv6 parsing.** `forwarded-headers.ts` now uses `normalizeIpAddress` from `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` instead of `split(":")[0]`. Bracketed / unbracketed / port-suffixed IPv6 literals all normalize correctly. Regression tests added for IPv6 contradiction detection and matching-across-forms.
4. **[P2] Public config contract completed.** `gateway.security` plus its three leaf fields now have entries in `schema.labels.ts`, `schema.tags.ts`, and `schema.help.ts` (all ≥80 chars with operational guidance, per `schema.help.quality.test.ts`).

Net diff: +50/-40 prod LOC across 8 files. The PR got smaller, not larger. All unit tests (`verify-client`: 8/8, `schema.help.quality`: 22/22) and `tsgo` core typecheck are green on the new head.

target.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded after-compaction hooks need a safe way to request a fresh session after compaction. The unsafe version exposed the gateway reset service directly from inside the hook, which could await reset while the active embedded run was still executing the hook, and it let hook code pass arbitrary session keys.

This PR fixes the OpenClaw core lifecycle boundary by making `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)` current-session scoped and deferred. Hook code can request `"new"` or `"reset"`, but cannot name another session. The owning embedded-run or compaction lifecycle drains the queued request after hook dispatch / run execution has exited.

## Summary

- Replaces arbitrary-key hook reset with current-session-scoped `ctx.api.resetSession(reason?)`.
- Defers hook-requested resets until the owning lifecycle has left hook dispatch / embedded-run execution, avoiding the active-run self-wait path in the gateway reset service.
- Wires the deferred reset queue through run-level hooks, direct compaction after-hooks, and queued/context-engine-owned after-compaction hooks.
- Adds regression coverage for deferred execution, current-session binding, and overflow compaction hook API availability.

## Evidence

### Hatched Egg / Behavior Evidence

This is an OpenClaw core lifecycle fix, not a Remnic property-data fix. Remnic/context compaction exposed the symptom, but the missing boundary is in OpenClaw's embedded-agent hook/session reset API.

Live gateway evidence from `openclaw_gateway_1` on July 16, 2026 shows the deployed runtime lacked this API and cron runs kept retrying through overflow/compaction instead of getting a fresh session:

```text
[diagnostic] long-running session ... sessionKey=agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170... activeWorkKind=model_call cronJobId=discord-public-heartbeat
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: compaction completed for agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:59ea4170..., triggering session reset
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for sage-router/frontier; retrying prompt
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 2/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 3/3); attempting auto-compaction for sage-router/frontier
[plugins] remnic: api.resetSession not available - compaction reset requires OC fork with PR #29985. Session ... will continue without reset.
```

A later hourly `discord-public-heartbeat` cron run repeated the same pattern with a new run session key (`agent:discord-public:cron:discord-public-heartbeat:run:9c60c213...`): overflow, compaction, reset request, API unavailable, then prompt retry. That ties the observed cron retry loop to the missing OpenClaw hook API rather than to Remnic property data.

After this PR, the hook receives:

```ts
await hookContext.api.resetSession("new");
```

and OpenClaw queues a current-session-only reset request for the lifecycle owner to flush after hook dispatch / embedded-run execution. The hook cannot target another session key, and reset failures are logged without turning cron completion into a scheduler retry.

### Live Rollout Proof

I applied the same reset-queue behavior to two real `openclaw_gateway_1` runtimes that were on `2026.6.11`.

target.title: fix(sandbox): cancel CDP probe response bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sandbox browser startup could leave HTTP response streams open after CDP readiness probes. Both unsuccessful probes that continued the retry loop and successful probes that returned early left unread response bodies for garbage collection, which could retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForSandboxCdp` now cancels every probe response body before branching on the HTTP status. Successful probes, retry timing, auth headers, and startup timeout behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Sandbox browser auto-start keeps the same readiness and failure semantics, while each completed CDP probe promptly releases its connection instead of leaving an unread stream open.

## Evidence

**Real-machine before / premise / after / negative control**

Environment: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic x86_64, Node v24.5.0.

I ran the same production-function harness from an `upstream/main` snapshot and this branch. The harness starts a real localhost `node:http` server, sends a streaming HTTP response through real Node fetch, calls the production `waitForSandboxCdp` loop, and observes the server-side TCP socket 250 ms after the function returns:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-before 200
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-after 200
node --import tsx /tmp/sandbox-cdp-body-cancel-proof.mts /tmp/sandbox-cdp-after 503
```

The harness loads the probe loop from `src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts` (mirrored in `/tmp/sandbox-cdp-probe-*.ts` for import isolation). The server never ends its response body, making socket closure a direct observation of consumer cancellation rather than normal body completion.

Negative control / before (`upstream/main` at `e01027dd28a`), streaming HTTP 200:

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":200,"cdpReachable":true,"serverObservedSocketClose":false}
```

After (`aac0533a40b`), streaming HTTP 200 and 503:

```text
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":200,"cdpReachable":true,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
{"productionFunction":"waitForSandboxCdp","status":503,"cdpReachable":false,"serverObservedSocketClose":true}
```

The unchanged `cdpReachable` values are the behavioral controls: successful probes still succeed and unsuccessful probes still fail, while the real server observes prompt connection release in both paths.

Premise: Undici 8.5.0, installed by this repository, documents that every response body must be consumed or canceled because Node garbage collection does not release connection resources promptly. This probe only needs the response status, so cancellation is the bounded cleanup operation.

Focused validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts -t "CDP probe response body"
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       4 passed | 46 skipped (50)

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/agents/sandbox/browser.ts src/agents/sandbox/browser.create.test.ts
exit 0

git diff --check
exit 0
```

Full build and broader suites were not run locally; fork GitHub Actions cover the wider gates. This is a non-visual transport cleanup, so no screenshot is applicable.

target.title: fix(mcp): doctor probes no longer start every server at once
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw mcp doctor --probe` would start a connection or stdio process for every configured MCP server at once. Large registries could therefore create an unbounded burst of external work during a single doctor run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor action now runs at most four per-server checks concurrently through the existing bounded task helper. Results remain sorted by server name, and unexpected check failures still propagate instead of being converted into successful doctor output. This is a focused operation bound; it adds no configuration or broader runtime refactor.

## User Impact

Operators can probe large MCP registries without `mcp doctor` launching every server simultaneously. All configured servers are still checked and reported in the same deterministic order.

## Scope and Competition Check

A fresh semantic open-PR scan on the pinned main snapshot found no equivalent fix. In particular, #103970 repairs legacy disabled-server migration in the top-level doctor/config flow, #108676 prevents disabled MCP servers from spawning, and #108104 isolates per-server runtime failures; none bounds the checks started by `openclaw mcp doctor --probe`.

The change is limited to doctor-action scheduling and regression coverage. It does not change MCP runtime defaults, configuration, public APIs, transport behavior, or ordinary agent MCP concurrency.

## Evidence

Regression proof before the production change:

```text
bounds concurrent MCP doctor server checks
expected 6 to be 4
```

Focused verification after the change:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
27 passed

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/mcp-cli.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
passed

pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/cli/mcp-cli.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

Real stdio behavior proof ran the actual `mcp doctor --probe --json` action in a separate process against six configured MCP SDK servers. Each server was a real child process held at its initialization boundary until the harness released it:

```json
{
  "configuredServers": 6,
  "starts": 6,
  "startsBeforeRelease": 4,
  "peakActive": 4,
  "allServersOk": true,
  "orderedNames": [
    "server-0",
    "server-1",
    "server-2",
    "server-3",
    "server-4",
    "server-5"
  ],
  "endEvents": 6,
  "livePidsAfter": []
}
```

This covers the production CLI action, per-server runtime creation, real stdio spawn, MCP SDK handshake, catalog collection, and runtime disposal.

Not covered: a live remote vendor MCP endpoint over HTTP/SSE. The near-real proof uses six actual local stdio MCP SDK servers so concurrency and child cleanup are deterministic without third-party credentials. The remaining risk is limited to scheduling: each existing per-server check is unchanged, and tests cover ordered results plus unexpected-error propagation.

target.title: fix(codex): skip runtime binding store when state API is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `@openclaw/codex` enabled, a typo like `openclaw stats --deep` previously printed `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'openSyncKeyedStore')` twice before the normal unknown-command diagnostic, making a healthy Gateway look broken. Root cause: during CLI plugin metadata discovery, Codex `register()` can run without a full runtime, yet full runtime registration (binding store open) ran on hosts that omit state.

Closes #107219.

## Summary

- Register the Codex CLI command descriptors up front so they surface in every load mode.
- Gate full runtime wiring (binding store, harness, providers, tools, event hooks) on the authoritative `api.registrationMode !== "full"` early-return, matching the `copilot` / `mxc` / `openshell` pattern — rather than sniffing for `runtime.state.openSyncKeyedStore`.
- Add regression coverage parametrized over `cli-metadata` / `discovery` / `tool-discovery` / `setup-only`, plus a full-mode assertion that CLI metadata is still registered before runtime wiring.

## Why registrationMode (addressing review)

Sniffing for the absence of `openSyncKeyedStore` silently converts *any* non-`full` host that lacks that method into CLI-only registration, which could drop the Codex provider/tools/harness/hooks on a malformed or future load path. `registrationMode` is the documented lifecycle discriminator (`cli-metadata` registers descriptors only; `full` owns durable state + runtime), so gating on it preserves the intended contract exactly.

## Evidence

`pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/index.test.ts` — **25 passed**.

Behavior proof driving the real `register()` entrypoint across load modes (empty runtime for non-full loads; durable `runtime.state` for full):

```
=== #107219 Codex register() behavior proof ===
-- metadata/discovery loads (empty runtime, pre-fix crashed here) --
mode=cli-metadata   threw=no  calls={"registerCli":1}
mode=discovery      threw=no  calls={"registerCli":1}
```

target.title: fix(ai): preserve Unicode in provider error body truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider error bodies containing emoji or other multi-byte Unicode characters at the 4000-character truncation boundary would produce lone surrogate code units (mojibake) in user-visible error messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The error body truncation in `formatProviderError` used raw `String.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH)` which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs. This replaces it with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core`, which is already used by other modules in `packages/ai` (`tool-result-text.ts`, `mistral.ts`).

## User Impact

Provider error messages displayed to users will no longer contain garbled Unicode characters when the error body contains emoji at or near the truncation boundary.

## Evidence

### Tests (7 passed, 1 file)
```
 ✓ formats an HTTP error with JSON body
 ✓ formats an HTTP error with text body
 ✓ formats an HTTP error with no body
 ✓ preserves SDK message that already contains the body
 ✓ excludes surrogate pair cleanly at 4000-char boundary
 ✓ preserves emoji entirely within truncation limit
 ✓ does not truncate body shorter than limit
```

### Test Coverage
- **Straddling surrogate pair**: Places 🦞 (U+1F99E, 2 code units) straddling the 4000-char boundary. Asserts no lone high surrogate (0xD800–0xDBFF) remains before `... [truncated]` — the test that would have FAILED with raw `.slice()`.
- **Emoji within limit**: Places 🦞 at indices 3996–3997, verifies full emoji appears in truncated output.
- **Short body**: Body ≤ 4000 chars passes through without truncation marker.

### Mechanical Correctness
- `truncateUtf16Safe` is dependency-free and already used by sibling modules in `packages/ai/`
- No behavior change for ASCII-only error bodies
